Why choose the Department of Materials Science & Engineering?
Ranked #1 in Canada, U of T's Department of Materials Science & Engineering empowers students to tackle global challenges through advanced materials - the enabler of all technologies.
Learn from world-renowned researchers, explore cutting-edge materials, and join a community of innovators shaping the future through advanced technology and impactful solutions.

Degree Programs
Master of Engineering
(MEng)
This course-based professional program provides an advanced, industry-oriented degree in as little as one year of full-time study.
Full-time, extended full-time, part-time and co-op options available.
Learn more about our MEng program
Master of Applied Science
(MASc)
This two-year research-intensive program includes a thesis project under the supervision of a faculty member.
The MASc is an excellent stepping stone to a doctoral degree.
Learn more about our MASc program
Doctor of Philosophy
(PhD)
The most advanced research degree offered.
Working with a faculty supervisor, PhD students engage in original research that contributes to their field of study.
Learn more about our PhD program

How to Apply
1
Check the admission requirements for your desired program, including English facility requirements.
2
Ensure you are aware of application deadlines. International student deadlines may be different from deadlines for domestic students.
3
If applying to a research-intensive program (MASc or PhD), consider connecting with potential supervisors within the MSE department.
4
Submit an application through U of T's School of Graduate Studies (SGS) after reviewing the details on how to apply.

The program also provides an option to combine the courses with a research project, allowing students to gain theoretical knowledge while participating in cutting-edge research projects."

Finances
Tuition information
Tuition varies based on your degree of interest. Visit U of T Engineering's Graduate Studies website to view program fees.
View tuition information
Funding
Graduate students may be eligible for a variety of scholarships, awards and financial aid .
MASc and PhD students are guaranteed funding to support them for the normal program length (e.g., 2 years for MASc, 4 years for PhD, 5 years for direct PhD entry.)
All graduate students are eligible to apply for Teaching Assistantship (TA) positions.
Frequently Asked Questions
What are your academic admissions requirements?Expand
Master of Engineering (MEng) - a Bachelor of Applied Science (BASc) in Engineering or Bachelor of Engineering (BEng) with a minimum of B (73%+) over the final two (2) years of an undergraduate program from an accredited institution
Master of Applied Science (MASc) - a Bachelor of Applied Science (BASc) in Engineering or Bachelor of Engineering (BEng) with a minimum average of B+ (78%+) over the final two (2) years of an undergraduate program from an accredited institution
Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) - successful completion of a research master's degree in engineering, with an overall average of at least B+ (78%+), from an accredited institution. Current MASc students within our department can apply to fast-track into the PhD program before completing the MASc degree requirements.
View all application requirements »
I am a prospective student from a non-Canadian institution; how do I know if my education background meet the admissions requirements?Expand
Applicants educated at non-Canadian institutions should note that their educational background will be assessed for equivalency with a University of Toronto degree.
Use the U of T International Degree Equivalency Tool to see which international credentials are required for master's and doctoral admission.
Do you have any English Language Facility requirements?Expand
All applicants holding degrees from universities outside Canada must demonstrate facility in English.
Please visit the Admission Requirements section for more information.
How do I apply?Expand
All applications for graduate studies at the University of Toronto are submitted online; no paper applications are available.
Please visit our How-to-Apply section for additional information.
Do I need to submit GRE scores?Expand
No. GRE scores are not required for application to graduate studies in Materials Science & Engineering at the University of Toronto.
Note that while the online application provides a field for GRE scores, do not submit GRE scores.
What is the tuition for graduate studies in Materials Science & Engineering (MSE) at U of T? Expand
Please visit our Finances section for additional information.
Is there funding for graduate studies in MSE at U of T?Expand
MASc and PhD students are automatically provided with guaranteed funding for the first two (2) years of the MASc program and the first four (4) years of the PhD program. Funding is not guaranteed beyond Year 2 of the MASc program nor beyond Year 4 of the PhD program.
MEng students are not eligible for the guaranteed funding package or any Departmental Scholarships/Fellowships or research stipends.
All tuition and related fees are the responsibility of the student. Please visit our Finances section for additional information.
Do I need to acquire a supervisor before applying?Expand
Prior to applying for MASc or PhD, students are encouraged to contact professors within the MSE department to determine whether or not they have the resources, interest or relevant research focus to accept you as a graduate student.
Students who are unable to make satisfactory contact are still encouraged to apply; applications from those who meet the minimum admission requirements are shared with MSE professors for review.
Please note: Expression of interest from a professor does NOT constitute an offer of admission. Official offers of admission are issued by the MSE Department once the graduate admissions committee has reviewed all applicants.
Do I need to submit official transcripts from all the universities I have attended?Expand
You will need to upload official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended. While the application review process begins with scanned transcripts from ALL the universities you attended, we will require original, hardcopy, sealed transcripts only if we offer you admission.
Please note that photocopies will NOT be accepted. Please visit the How-to-Apply section for more information. Do NOT submit original, hardcopy transcripts unless the MSE Department requests you to do so.
Does my undergraduate degree (for MASc/MEng application) or master's degree (for PhD application) need to be an engineering, or specifically, an MSE degree?Expand
No. Applicants with a background in pure and/or applied sciences are encouraged to consider MSE. However, your previous degree(s) must demonstrate applicable and transferable knowledge relevant to graduate studies in our Department.
Furthermore, the extent to which your background aligns with the research interests of our professor(s) will also influence your application. All applications are assessed on a case-by-case basis by the MSE Graduate Admissions Committee.
